transcript.text: The hospital was in my network. Why do I owe $2,310 for anesthesia?

Good question, and you're right to ask. Your surgery was at an in-network hospital, but the anesthesia provider was out of network. Federal surprise-billing protections generally limit what you can be billed in that situation to your in-network cost-sharing, which Aetna calculated as $420.00. The $2,310 statement balance looks like it's above that, so I can't ask for payment on it as stated. I'm placing a hold so statements and reminders stop, and I'm sending this to our billing staff to review and correct the balance. They're available Mon-Fri 8am-5pm Central. You don't need to pay anything right now.
So what do I actually owe?

Based on Aetna's explanation of benefits, your cost-sharing for this service is $420.00. That's the most you should owe, and it's the only part that looks clearly owed. The other $1,890 of the statement balance shouldn't be billed to you.

I haven't taken any payment, and you don't have to pay anything today. Staff will review the account and correct the balance, and they can confirm the final amount and set up the $420.00 payment once it's fixed. If you'd like to pay that part now, I can send a link. Would you like that?
